newsitem.title: CANADA: Thai banker to face Canada extradition hearing.
newsitem.headline: Thai banker to face Canada extradition hearing.

text.p: A former Thai bank official arrested on fraud charges in Canada will face extradition proceedings starting Oct. 30, a Canadian court ruled on Wednesday.
Rakesh Saxena, a former treasury advisor to the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce, was arrested near Vancouver in July by Canadian and Thai police.
Saxena, 45, an Indian national and resident of Thailand, is accused of colluding with a group of other bank executives in embezzling $63.3 million. He has denied the charges.
Justice Jon Sigurdson set the date for Saxena's extradition proceeding at a brief British Columbia Supreme Court hearing on Wednesday in Vancouver.
Saxena, who was an independent treasury adviser to the bank, was granted bail following his arrest on condition that he post C$1.25 million (US$909,000) in bond and surrender his passport.

At least four bank employees, including its president, have appeared before the courts in Thailand and were released on bail. The Thai government took control of the bank in May after it faced a public run on deposits.
The country's central bank has said that the Bangkok Bank of Commerce has more than $3 billion of bad, risky and non-performing loans.
